reasoning: Both are correct and handle bad input well. A reads the grid and ground from the real Baseplate and uses the engine's overlap query, which handles rotated parts, models and any other parts in the folder. Its comments are leaner and it passes every check. B hardcodes the ground and grid origin, uses an unrotated-only box test, has a long usage header, and fails the comment convention. B's snapFromSurface helper is nice, but it does not outweigh these issues.

criteria.note: All five types via BLOCK_TYPES, snapAxis aligned to the Baseplate corner and getGroundY top, 0 to 200 height with EPSILON, 24-stud reach from HumanoidRootPart, GetPartBoundsInBox shrunk by EPSILON*2 so adjacent blocks are allowed, short reasons, and snapPosition is public.
typeof checks on blockType and position come before isFiniteNumber (catches NaN and ±huge), and all of it runs before any snapping or range check.
The NaN, 32-bit float and EPSILON comments explain why; the PlacementContext field comments ('Holds every placed block; checked for overlaps.') mostly restate the field.
Mostly tight, but the file-level section banners are verbose and the snapPosition doc runs to two paragraphs.
snapPosition and validatePlacement docs cover boundary behavior, the hit-offset advice and that the function never errors, without listing parameters; the first is a little long.
No history, no references to the request, no pointers to outside documents.
One strict-typed shared module with no remote or UI, a PlacementResult union type, and every check passes.
Rules work, but GROUND_Y = 0 and the X/Z grid origin are hardcoded rather than read from the Baseplate, and the hand-written box test assumes unrotated blocks.
isValidBlockType checks the type first, isFinite uses comparisons that reject NaN and inf, and the 'not <=' reach check adds another guard.
The GROUND_Y explanation, OVERLAP_EPSILON reason, isFinite note and 'not <=' rationale are good; the usage example in the header is tutorial text rather than why-comments.
The 15-line header with a usage example and client instructions is long for a module comment.
snap, snapFromSurface and check have useful docs on return meaning and failure behavior; isValidBlockType has none, which is fine since it is obvious.
No history or references to the request.
Shared module, no remote or UI, typed; but it fails the double-hyphen comment convention on line 11 and exports extra constants.

strengths: Reads the ground height and grid origin from the real Baseplate instead of hardcoding them
Engine overlap query is robust to rotated parts and models, and only searches the blocks folder
Clean typed result union with short reasons
Passes all checks, including the comment conventions
weaknesses: Section banners and a few field comments add bulk
No ready-made helper for snapping from a surface hit (only described in a doc comment)

strengths: snapFromSurface helper gives the client a ready path from raycast to cell
Frozen module and frozen block-type list
weaknesses: Hardcoded GROUND_Y and X/Z origin break if the Baseplate moves
Hand-written box test ignores rotation and skips other instance types
Long usage header; fails the comment convention check
